text: A standalone bootable x86-64 operating system that runs Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B directly on hardware or KVM with no Linux, no Windows, no C, no Rust, and no libc . Running live on a diskless ( 0 GB storage) Proxmox VE VM booted from the hybrid BIOS+UEFI ISO (Intel Xeon E5-2670 v3, 12 cores, 2 GiB RAM): sudo apt install nasm binutils qemu-system-x86 Optional, for building a bootable BIOS+UEFI hybrid ISO ( make os-iso ): sudo apt install grub-pc-bin grub-efi-amd64-bin grub-common mtools xorriso An exported models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin file ( --scale-dtype fp16 v2 recommended, or legacy v1 --scale-dtype fp32 ; see Phase 1 setup ). Build From the repository root ( FAST_Q8=1 is enabled by default; pass FAST_Q8=0 for legacy FP32-activation mode): make os FAST_Q8=1 make os-check Expected output ( FAST_Q8=1 ): -rwxr-xr-x 1 user user 24252 build/asm-llm-os.elf build/asm-llm-os.elf: ELF 32-bit LSB executable, Intel 80386, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, stripped There is no dynamic section in this file. (The kernel is linked as 64-bit ELF and wrapped into ELF32 via objcopy -O elf32-i386 for standard Multiboot 1 loaders like QEMU -kernel and GRUB2; boot.asm transitions immediately into 64-bit Long Mode.) Boot directly in the terminal over COM1 serial ( -nographic ): qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -m 2G -smp 16 \ -kernel build/asm-llm-os.elf \ -initrd models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin \ -nographic Or use the Makefile shortcut: make os-run MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin SMP=16 Run a one-shot batch prompt with clean ACPI shutdown: make os-run MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin SMP=16 \ CMDLINE= ' prompt="Explain how a CPU cache works in 3 concise sentences." max_tokens=64 think=0 shutdown=1 ' Open a live 80x25 VGA GUI window with PS/2 keyboard input: qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -m 2G -smp 16 \ -kernel build/asm-llm-os.elf \ -initrd models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin \ -vga std -serial stdio Option B: Bootable Hybrid BIOS+UEFI ISO Packages the 23 KB kernel, GRUB2 Multiboot 1 config, and the 649 MiB .asmbin model into a single self-contained ~661 MiB bootable ISO ( build/asm-llm-os.iso ): make os-iso MODEL=models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin Boot the ISO in QEMU KVM (SeaBIOS or UEFI OVMF): # Legacy BIOS (SeaBIOS) qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -m 2G -smp 16 \ -cdrom build/asm-llm-os.iso -nographic # UEFI (OVMF) qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -m 2G -smp 16 \ -bios /usr/share/ovmf/OVMF.fd \ -cdrom build/asm-llm-os.iso -nographic Option C: Deploying on Proxmox VE (0 GB Disk VM) Because the entire OS and model live inside the ISO and run out of RAM, the VM needs zero hard disks . qm create 250 \ --name asm-llm-os \ --machine pc \ --bios seabios \ --cpu host \ --cores 12 \ --memory 2048 \ --balloon 0 \ --vga std \ --serial0 socket \ --ide2 local:iso/asm-llm-os.iso,media=cdrom \ --boot order=ide2 qm start 250 Interact either through the Proxmox web UI ( noVNC Console , VGA + PS/2 keyboard) or over the virtual serial port: qm terminal 250 (Note: --cpu host is required so the VM exposes AVX2 + FMA, and --balloon 0 ensures 2 GiB of contiguous guest RAM for the 649 MiB model + 449 MiB KV-cache arena.) By default, the bare-metal console runs in multi-turn chat mode with persistent KV-cache : each new user turn prefills only the new Qwen3 chat tokens starting at g_chat_pos without recomputing earlier turns, closes every assistant turn in the KV-cache with <|im_end|>\n , and displays live context usage ( ctx=X/2048 ) in the decode stats line. When the KV-cache approaches max_seq ( pos + n_prompt + 64 >= max_seq ), it prints [chat] context full, resetting KV-cache and resets cleanly. If booted with prompt="..." and shutdown=0 , the initial batch turn stays in the KV-cache so you can continue the same conversation in the REPL. Both PS/2 keyboard (VGA) and COM1 serial ( 115200 8N1 ) are polled simultaneously. Type any message and press Enter, or use a built-in command: Pass via QEMU -append "..." , make os-run CMDLINE='...' , or make os-iso CMDLINE='...' : Phase 2 compiles the exact same shared/math.asm , shared/matmul.asm , shared/tokenizer.asm , and shared/transformer.asm with -DBARE_METAL -DFAST_Q8=$(FAST_Q8) and pairs them with 4,167 lines of bare-metal OS code: python3 scripts/verify_os.py --model models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.asmbin --run-dir runs/os-verify All 5 parity prompts (English technical, English concise, Russian UTF-8, arithmetic word problem, --think mode) match Phase 1 ( build/asm-llm ) 100% exact in prompt tokens, generated tokens, and raw UTF-8 bytes. (Because boot.asm identity-maps guest RAM with 2 MiB huge pages, the bare-metal kernel avoids 4 KiB page-table walks across the 614 MiB model and outperforms both Linux mmap() Phase 1 and llama.cpp CPU Q8_0 at every thread count.)
